Question Choices: Fill: A father is 4 times as old as his son. In 10 years, the father will be 3 times as old as the son. How old is the son now?
Solution: x is the son’s current age and y the father’s. Add 10 to BOTH current ages before comparing their future ages. System: y=4 × x; y+10=3 × (x+10). Isolate y: y=(4)x+(0). Substitute into the other equation: (-3)x+(1)[(4)x+(0)]=20. Combine: (1)x=20, so x=20. Then y=(4)(20)+(0)=80. Check both equations: -4(20)+1(80)=0; -3(20)+1(80)=20. Requested answer: 20.

Question Choices: Fill: A father is three times as old as his daughter. In 4 years, their total age will be 52. How old is the father now?
Solution: x is the daughter’s current age and y the father’s. The future sum adds 4 years twice. System: y=3 × x; (y+4)+(x+4)=52. Isolate y: y=(3)x+(0). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(3)x+(0)]=44. Combine: (4)x=44, so x=11. Then y=(3)(11)+(0)=33. Check both equations: -3(11)+1(33)=0; 1(11)+1(33)=44. Requested answer: 33.

Question Choices: Fill: A mother is 8 years older than twice her daughter's age. Their total age is 50. How old is the daughter?
Solution: x is the daughter’s age and y the mother’s. System: y=2 × x+8; x+y=50. Isolate y: y=(2)x+(8). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(2)x+(8)]=50. Combine: (3)x=42, so x=14. Then y=(2)(14)+(8)=36. Check both equations: -2(14)+1(36)=8; 1(14)+1(36)=50. Requested answer: 14.

Question Choices: Fill: A student walks from home to school at 4 km/h and returns by bike at 12 km/h. Total travel time is 2 hours. What is the one-way distance in km?
Solution: x is the shared one-way distance. Add outbound and return travel times, distance divided by the matching speed. x/4+x/12=2. The coefficient of x is 1/3, so x=6 km. Substitute this distance into BOTH time terms to recover the stated total. Requested answer: 6.

Question Choices: Fill: A number is split into two parts. The larger part is 5 more than twice the smaller. Their sum is 41. Find the larger part.
Solution: x is the smaller part and y the larger. System: y=2 × x+5; x+y=41. Isolate y: y=(2)x+(5). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(2)x+(5)]=41. Combine: (3)x=36, so x=12. Then y=(2)(12)+(5)=29. Check both equations: -2(12)+1(29)=5; 1(12)+1(29)=41. Requested answer: 29.
